title: Treaty of Rapallo (Germany–Soviet Russia, 1922)
summary: Germany and Soviet Russia signed a treaty at Rapallo, Italy, resuming diplomatic and consular relations. Both sides waived war-related financial claims and agreed to most-favoured-nation treatment in trade. As Germany's first agreement as an independent agent since World War I, it angered the Western Allies.

as_recorded.value: Original text done in duplicate at Rapallo on April 16, 1922

importance.justification: Reshaped postwar diplomacy by restoring German–Soviet relations and alarming the Western Allies.
